citations.quote: QuickSAT/step_SATdb, is a collaborative, design, validation, test and manufacturing Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) environment for application in a range of space vehicles including CubeSATs through 1000+ kg class satellites.

For the past 5 years Sci Zone in conjunction with AFRL Kirtland and NASA Ames Research Center developed our innovative Satellite Design Automation - Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) environment QuickSAT $ ^{\mathrm{TM}} $ , in conjunction with our step_SATdb open source database architecture.

step_SATdb allows for the exchange of data between existing design tools such as MATLAB, SINDA, SOAP and QuickSAT $ ^{\mathrm{TM}} $ , and provides a data architecture tracking requirements, hardware and software components in inventory, and tracks the variations of satellite configurations and supporting revisions to the analysis done for each configuration.

QuickSAT $ ^{\mathrm{TM}} $ is a web based environment supporting the design process via its integrated analysis and information management tools and integration to existing design tools. QuickSAT also provides coherency between a range of applications and data sets.

step_SATdb stores and distributes the supporting satellite design, configuration, mission, support and test data from a centralized database server and can distribute the data across multiple platforms and via the internet.

The key advantage of the step_SATdb for the U.S. Government, universities and the aerospace industry is that the architecture is open source and utilizes a host of standards and open environments including Java, HTML5, php and MySQL. This provides for not only a low cost software development environment for everyone in the community, but also a standard interface for software development and for the exchange of data. This represents a real savings to the government.
Parts in use cannot be deleted or modified, however new versions can be created. Parts not in use can be modified. The step_SATdb also tracks availability, time to build, quantity in stock and TRL.

"Satellite knowledge" is organized on several levels in the QuickSAT/step_SATdb environment as shown in Figure 3. It starts with organizing the entire project in a mission. A mission stores everything related to the project - this starts with the satellite configuration. You can have as many satellite configurations within a mission.

A configuration stores the physical configuration of a satellite - system components and subsystems, component location and orientation within a satellite, launch vehicle information and power and propulsion elements at the satellite level.

Within QuickSAT/step_SATdb you can view all variations of the satellite configuration and trace the evolution of the design including who assembled it and revised a configuration and when the configuration was generated. You can compare configurations and study trends and changes. All historical data from each configuration is maintained through out the project lifetime and beyond - hence for the controls in QuickSAT/step_SATdb to prevent changes to parts that are in use.

For each configuration there can be several revisions to the analysis. You can modify analytical models several times for a given configuration and save each one for comparison. Each revision maintains a flight plan that defines all flight legs and phases of flight plus the modes of operation and the active modes of operation for each flight leg.

Each flight leg then tracks to a set of analysis tools - internal and external. This includes link analysis, power analysis, thermal analysis, ACDS, and orbit modeling to name a few. As a flight plan is modified all related analytical data is modified and tracked with the flight plan changes.

Consider the example of the EarthSCAN formation flying mission. The EarthSCAN formation flying mission is designed to be carried on board as a single "package" as a secondary payload on a larger launch vehicle. The launch vehicle interface consists of three payload interfaces - one for the EarthSCAN "mother ship", EarthSCAN-M, and two side by side P-POD launchers for EarthSCAN cubeSAT satellites C-1 and C-2.

To edit and add a flight leg, an orbit or an orbit change/trajectory, and re-arrange flight legs one selects the Edit Flight Plan button. Figure 5 shows the Edit Flight Plan screen. Here flight leg information can be modified. Changes to the flight information are propagated to all the analysis tools.

QuickSAT will calculate orbital parameters such as eccentricity, orbit period, time in eclipse and in the case of a trajectory calculate the $ \Delta \mathrm{V} $ , a term that is correlated directly with the QuickSAT Propulsion Module.

The QuickSAT Flight Planning module not only works for Earth based missions, but missions to planets, asteroids, comets, and in Solar orbit. The stepSATdb Repository stores all related planetary data in addition to ground stations, cities and launch vehicles.
For EP systems, the user would separately track the power bounds within the power module.

The QuickSAT/step_SATdb PLM environment stores and distributes the supporting satellite design, configuration, mission, manufacturing and test data from a centralized database/cloud environment and can distribute the data across multiple platforms and via the internet.
QuickSAT/step_SATdb is an open source data environment that is extensible, multiplatform and allows for internal and external analytical modules to be added.
step_SATdb as a data cloud brings together customers, designers, technicians and vendors, all of which leads to the efficient launch and deployment of a satellite (see Figure 2). $ ^{5} $
